lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The target role is unclear and the resume presents product, operations, and diesel-mechanic profiles.
items.because: The current mechanical role can dominate the reader's interpretation despite the strong product evidence.

items.says: Harbor Payments should appear above Crestline in reverse-chronological order.
items.because: The internship ended after the Crestline role.

items.says: Verify that the portfolio or LinkedIn URL is live and complete.
Make sure the website supports the product story rather than serving as a placeholder.
Clarify that the MBA was completed.
items.because: The listed graduation date has passed.

items.says: Add a strong concentration, relevant coursework, academic distinction, or leadership experience if it supports the target role.
Make the MBA's overlap with the internship and projects easy to follow.
items.because: The overlapping dates should be intentional and credible.

items.says: Make the mechanic role's relevance deliberate by emphasizing product-transferable work or fleet reliability, turnaround, compliance, and process control.
items.because: The current job is not aligned on its face with product management.

items.says: Clarify whether the under-five-day figure is an average, maximum, or target.
State whether the turnaround time improved on a prior baseline.
Add evidence of planning, prioritization, troubleshooting, documentation, coordination, or process improvement if applicable.
items.because: Those details would make the work more relevant to product or operations roles.

items.says: Avoid implying that you alone caused the turnaround result unless that attribution is supportable.
The bullet is too responsibility-focused and needs an operational result.
items.because: It does not show inspection performance, avoided downtime, reliability, compliance, or the scale covered.

items.says: Connect logging service records to audit readiness, regulatory compliance, maintenance planning, or reliability.
items.because: Logging records alone is a low-impact activity.

items.says: The scorecard bullet lacks an outcome or decision enabled by the work.
items.because: It only describes what was owned and discussed.

items.says: Add the number of carriers, managers, lanes, or regions covered.
items.because: The bullet does not show scale.

items.says: Specify whether the 30% reduction is relative or in percentage points.
Add the baseline error rate if available.
Add an operational consequence such as fewer claims, less rework, or improved order accuracy.
Clarify the forecast-error metric and product scope.
Describe the change from 18% to 11% precisely as seven percentage points or a 38.9% relative reduction.
Confirm that the 12 quarters reflect the candidate's actual ownership period.
items.because: They should not merely represent the total time the process existed.

items.says: The route-planning bullet contains too many separate accomplishments and is difficult to scan.
items.because: It combines rollout, SOP rewriting, driver training, and vendor negotiations.

items.says: Add the financial value of the 1,800 annual driver hours saved if it can be calculated credibly.
State the outcome of the vendor negotiations.
items.because: Taking over negotiations describes an action rather than contract savings, improved terms, or another result.

items.says: For product roles, emphasize adoption, requirements, rollout management, stakeholder coordination, and measurable usage or operational impact.
Give the Harbor Payments internship more prominence.
items.because: It is the most directly relevant product experience.

items.says: Clarify whether the time-to-first-payment reduction was statistically or operationally significant.
Clarify whether the pilot result led to the broader rollout and how this differs from the rollout evidence in line 21.
items.because: The onboarding bullets should be clearly related without becoming repetitive.

items.says: Clarify the experiment population.
State whether the conversion result was statistically significant.
Distinguish the test population from the later all-merchant rollout.
Characterize the change from 61% to 66% as five percentage points, not necessarily 5%.
Support the claim that the flow was shipped to all merchants with scope and timing.
Defining Reach as the number of support tickets a feature would close is not the standard meaning of Reach in RICE.
items.because: Reach usually means the users, customers, or transactions affected over a defined period.

items.says: If support tickets were a proxy for Reach, make that methodology explicit.
Show that the other RICE components were actually applied.
State the decision or result produced by the prioritization.
items.because: Naming a framework alone is not strong evidence of product judgment.

items.says: The bullet is too process-heavy and should reduce the intermediate steps.
items.because: The decision and impact should be emphasized.

items.says: The bullet duplicates roadmap-prioritization evidence from line 18.
items.because: The Harbor section has multiple bullets about the same competency.

items.says: Add the business consequence, such as projected loss reduction, expected support reduction, the selected initiative, or an executive decision.
The checkout A/B-test bullet is substantially redundant with line 17.
items.because: It repeats the same conversion result.

items.says: The wording about an effect on merchants' customers is confusing and should match the actual experimental unit and population.
items.because: The experiment appears to have been randomized by session.

items.says: If retained, include the sample size, confidence or significance information, and actual unit of analysis.
items.because: The bullet should demonstrate experimental-design rigor rather than repeat the result.

items.says: Make the funded rollout's scope more concrete with its timeline, merchant count, regions, or expected business impact.
Clarify the distinction between this organizational-adoption result and the onboarding execution in line 16.
items.because: The two bullets overlap slightly.

items.says: Clarify whether the 3,100 students are the eligible audience, registered users, reached audience, or active users.
Explain how the nine-tonne figure was measured if it is an estimate.
Make the first-year measurement period explicit and align it with the project dates.
items.because: The project began in October 2023 and is listed as ongoing.

items.says: The stated 150% increase is mathematically incorrect.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 750 users, or 187.5%.

items.says: Clarify whether reminders were the tested cause of the full user increase or merely one associated product change.
Add retention, notification engagement, repeat-pickup, or cohort data if available.
items.because: Those metrics would make the product impact more credible than a simple before-and-after comparison.

items.says: Describing the rise from 75% to 95% as a 20% increase uses incorrect percentage terminology.
items.because: It is a 20-percentage-point increase or a 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and whether the fill-rate improvement was sustained.
Add any improvement in availability, waste, or cancellations.
Clearly distinguish the $2.4M modeled opportunity from realized savings.
items.because: Sized savings were not yet achieved.

items.says: Add the model's main assumptions or implementation conditions if space allows.
Clarify the candidate's personal role in the financial model, operational analysis, stakeholder work, or recommendation process.
The patient-intake bullet is too passive and vague.
items.because: It is weaker than the rest of the resume.

items.says: Specify what changed and provide concrete evidence of adoption or operational results.
items.because: Saying the changes were adopted is not enough by itself.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome duplicates the approval already mentioned in line 28.
items.because: The two bullets should not claim the same outcome without distinct evidence.

items.says: Include any defined pilot scope, timeline, or success criteria.
Requirements writing is generic and should remain only if demonstrated through documentation, acceptance criteria, or delivery work.
Consider adding discovery, experimentation, analytics, prioritization, and stakeholder management when supported elsewhere.
Match the skills to target job descriptions rather than listing every method encountered.
The tools list is short for a product or operations candidate.
items.because: Relevant categories could include SQL, dashboarding, prototyping, survey, project-management, presentation, or financial-modeling tools actually used.

items.says: Include relevant tools used in the A/B testing, app, S&OP, or route-planning work.
